- [S1021] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Defines EEP = {E1..E8}: an eight-stage mandatory pipeline (Claim, Locate, Inspect, Trace, Test, Observe, Classify, Report) that an agent must explicitly state it performed (not necessarily at equal depth) before making an architectural claim; the governing principle is 'an agent must prove an architectural claim from evidence; it must not prove it from plausibility.'" (anchor: "Claim → Locate → Inspect → Trace → Test → Observe → Classify → Report")
- [S1021] types=[DEFINITION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E1 Claim requires a precise, falsifiable proposition (contrasts 'Understand KnowledgeOS' [bad] with a typed claim like 'AuthoritativeDecision -> Provenance' [good]) and distinguishes six claim types: Structural (component depends on component), Behavioral (creating an authoritative object requires provenance), Governance (only an authorized actor can approve), Temporal (superseded decisions excluded from current knowledge), Assurance (rule X deterministically verified), Operational (runtime state fed back into KnowledgeOS)." (anchor: "Structural / Behavioral / Governance / Temporal / Assurance / Operational")
- [S1021] types=[PRINCIPLE] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E2 Locate names search targets (README, docs/, ADR/, architecture/, src/, tests/, schemas/, migrations/, config/, CI/CD, hooks/, agents/, runtime configuration) and states the negative-evidence rule: finding nothing in one location does not prove system-wide absence; the agent must report 'no evidence found in the inspected locations' rather than 'the capability does not exist.'" (anchor: "NotFound(Location) ≠ Absent(System)")
- [S1021] types=[DISTINCTION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E3 Inspect distinguishes evidence types by artifact kind: documentation establishes DeclaredArchitecture, source code establishes ImplementedArchitecture, tests establish VerifiedBehavior — these are different evidence types and must not be conflated." (anchor: "DeclaredArchitecture ... ImplementedArchitecture ... VerifiedBehavior")
- [S1021] types=[PRINCIPLE, FORMALIZATION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E4 Trace: given a claim Decision -> Implementation, the agent follows the chain Decision -> ADR/record -> change request -> PR -> commit -> artifact -> deployment, aiming at semantic linkage rather than textual name-matching; defines traceability-strength scale T0 (no link) < T1 (textual similarity) < T2 (explicit reference) < T3 (machine-readable identifier) < T4 (verified causal/implementation relationship), e.g. an ADR-042 identifier appearing in a commit is stronger evidence than shared wording." (anchor: "The objective is not simply finding matching names. It is establishing semantic linkage.")
- [S1021] types=[DEFINITION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E5 Test: for a behavioral claim (e.g. 'authoritative knowledge cannot be created without provenance'), execute a concrete test (create(authoritative=true, provenance=null) expecting Reject) and classify it on a six-level test hierarchy (Static, Unit, Integration, Architecture, Deployment, Runtime) since the test type affects what the result actually proves." (anchor: "Static / Unit / Integration / Architecture / Deployment / Runtime")
- [S1021] types=[PRINCIPLE] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E6 Observe: operational claims (e.g. 'Nexus runs rootless') require inspecting actual runtime/deployment/logs/metrics/events, not merely a static configuration file such as a Podman config." (anchor: "Static code is not enough for operational claims.")
- [S1021] types=[DEFINITION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E7 Classify: every finding receives one of four epistemic classifications — FACT (directly evidenced, e.g. a Containerfile using a specified base image, via E2/E3), INFERENCE (a reasoned interpretation that must not be presented as established fact without stronger evidence, e.g. 'this repo appears to implement the Evidence bounded context'), TARGET (intended future architecture unless implementation proves otherwise, e.g. 'KnowledgeOS should provide closed-loop governance'), GAP (Expected ≠ Observed, e.g. architecture requires provenance but authoritative records can currently be created without it)." (anchor: "FACT | INFERENCE | TARGET | GAP")
- [S1021] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "E8 Report: the final report must never collapse evidence into one narrative; it uses a fixed section format (Claim, Facts, Evidence, Inference, Verification, Gap, Target, Confidence) 'to prevent architectural contamination,' illustrated with a worked standard-agent-output example ending in STATUS: CONFORMANT / CONFIDENCE: HIGH." (anchor: "CLAIM / FACTS / EVIDENCE / INFERENCE / VERIFICATION / GAP / TARGET / CONFIDENCE")
- [S1021] types=[FORMALIZATION, ARGUMENT] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Proposes a five-level ordinal confidence scale (C0 Unknown .. C4 Verified) as superior to arbitrary percentages; argues LLMConfidence ≠ EvidenceConfidence because an LLM stating '95% confident' does not establish a quantitative probability, whereas evidence-derived confidence must derive from evidence quality; also distinguishes EvidenceStrength from Confidence (strong evidence can still leave interpretive ambiguity)." (anchor: "C0=Unknown, C1=Weak, C2=Moderate, C3=Strong, C4=Verified")
- [S1021] types=[PRINCIPLE] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "States an agent stopping rule / anti-hallucination rule: when evidence is insufficient the agent must preserve UNKNOWN rather than fill the gap from general knowledge; explicitly frames stopping with disclosed uncertainty (e.g. 'implementation is supported, enforcement is unverified') as a successful investigation, not a failure." (anchor: "If evidence is insufficient, the agent MUST preserve UNKNOWN.")
- [S1021] types=[CONCEPT] scope=METHODOLOGICAL — "Defines five repository investigation modes with distinct evidence focus — A Architecture reconstruction (Structure+Dependencies), B Governance verification (Authority+Decision+Process), C Assurance verification (Rule+Test+Evidence), D Runtime verification (Deployment+Observation), E Knowledge reconstruction (Meaning+Provenance+Validity) — and requires the agent to select the mode before searching, and to follow a Broad->Narrow->Exact->Trace search strategy (e.g. 'provenance' -> 'source_id' -> 'createKnowledge' -> tests -> runtime)." (anchor: "Mode A — Architecture reconstruction ... Mode E — Knowledge reconstruction")
